introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The time, $x$, in minutes spent by some 10 students to prepare for a test and the marks, $y$, which they scored are shown in the table below.

| Time, $x$ | 4 | 8 | 22 | 30 | 44 | 56 | 70 | 80 | 85 | 88 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marks, $y$ | 20 | 27 | 33 | 40 | 45 | 50 | 53 | 58 | 65 | 70 |

Given that $\sum x^2 = 32805$, $\sum y^2 = 23641$ and $\sum xy = 27037$,
incertitudes: Question 8 : les sommes imprimées ($\sum x^2 = 32805$, $\sum y^2 = 23641$, $\sum xy = 27037$) ont été recalculées sur le tableau et sont exactes ; $\sum x = 487$ et $\sum y = 461$ ne sont pas imprimées et sont calculées dans le corrigé.

Question 8 (b), (c) : $b = 0.5046$ et $a = 21.5236$ ; l'équation s'écrit $y = 21.52 + 0.5046x$ ; pour $x = 50$ le corrigé donne $46.76$ (soit environ 47 points) avec les coefficients non arrondis ($46.75$ avec les coefficients arrondis à 21.52 et 0.5046).
Question 8 : les points imprimés par partie, (9, 2, 2), totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) calculate, to 4 decimal places, the product moment correlation coefficient for these data and briefly explain what information your answer gives you about the relationship between $x$ and $y$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Here $n = 10$. First the totals from the table:

$$\sum x = 4 + 8 + 22 + 30 + 44 + 56 + 70 + 80 + 85 + 88 = 487, \qquad \sum y = 20 + 27 + 33 + 40 + 45 + 50 + 53 + 58 + 65 + 70 = 461$$

Then the sums of squares and products about the means:

$$S_{xx} = \sum x^2 - \frac{(\sum x)^2}{n} = 32805 - \frac{487^2}{10} = 32805 - 23716.9 = 9088.1$$

$$S_{yy} = \sum y^2 - \frac{(\sum y)^2}{n} = 23641 - \frac{461^2}{10} = 23641 - 21252.1 = 2388.9$$

$$S_{xy} = \sum xy - \frac{\sum x \sum y}{n} = 27037 - \frac{487 \times 461}{10} = 27037 - 22450.7 = 4586.3$$

The product moment correlation coefficient is

$$r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}\,S_{yy}}} = \frac{4586.3}{\sqrt{9088.1 \times 2388.9}} = \frac{4586.3}{4659.4} = 0.98430\ldots$$

**$r \approx 0.9843$.**

**Interpretation.** $r$ is positive and very close to $+1$, so there is a very strong positive linear correlation between $x$ and $y$: the more time a student spends preparing, the higher the mark, and the points lie very close to an upward-sloping straight line. (Correlation alone does not prove that the extra preparation time is the cause of the higher marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Find the equation of the regression line of $y$ on $x$ in the form $y = a + bx$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The regression line of $y$ on $x$ has gradient

$$b = \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}} = \frac{4586.3}{9088.1} = 0.50464\ldots \approx 0.5046$$

and passes through the mean point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$, where $\bar{x} = \dfrac{487}{10} = 48.7$ and $\bar{y} = \dfrac{461}{10} = 46.1$:

$$a = \bar{y} - b\bar{x} = 46.1 - 0.504649 \times 48.7 = 21.5236\ldots \approx 21.52$$

**The regression line of $y$ on $x$ is $y = 21.52 + 0.5046\,x$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) A student who spent 50 minutes preparing for the test could not write because of ill health.

Estimate the marks that this student would have scored if she wrote the test.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute $x = 50$ in the regression line of $y$ on $x$:

$$y = 21.5236 + 0.504649 \times 50 = 21.5236 + 25.2325 = 46.756\ldots$$

**The estimated mark is about $46.76$, that is about $47$ marks.**

This is a reliable estimate because $x = 50$ lies inside the range of the data ($4$ to $88$ minutes), so it is an interpolation, and $r$ is very close to $1$.
